title: Contour & Chroma Migration: introduce dynamic contour tokens and redesigned chromatic hierarchy
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Replace the brittle legacy color/spacing/radius/elevation token surface with a small set of composable 'contour' tokens and a chromatic hierarchy that can be interpolated for compact/comfortable density modes. Deliverables: Figma token file, tokens.json export for the component library, migration map for components (buttons, tables, charts, form controls), and a staged rollout plan (feature-flagged token layer + telemetry). This ticket covers the design spec and migration decisions; engineering tickets will split out the implementation per component.
acceptance_criteria: Figma token page with contour token set and chromatic ramp published and versioned
tokens.json exported and validated by the design token linter (no missing references)
Migration map (legacy -> contour tokens) completed for buttons, tables, charts and core form controls
Contrast checks: all foreground/background pairs meet WCAG 2.1 AA for regular text and 3.0 for large text where applicable
Prototype components (button, table row, card) implemented in Storybook using new tokens and validated by QA for visual regressions
Rollout plan approved by PM and Engineering with staged flags and telemetry metrics defined (render mismatch rate, dropped frames, uplift in a11y violations)
design_decisions: Use a small orthogonal token surface: contour-{level} for background layers, edge-{level} for borders, accent-{role} for brand/semantic accents. This reduces combinatorial explosion of tokens.
Chromatic hierarchy is defined as H0..H6 ramps per hue with an interpolation algorithm (LAB interpolation) to preserve perceived lightness when shifting tints or switching themes.
Introduce two density scales (compact, comfortable) implemented by scale multipliers applied to spacing/radius tokens instead of duplicating tokens for every component.
Elevation model moves from flat named shadows to a layered model: umbra, penumbra, ambient with tokenized offsets/blur/alpha. Ambient occlusion token exists for deep composition shadows.

Accessibility trade-off: tighter contrasts on compact mode are acceptable only when components use explicit focus/hover affordances; otherwise default to comfortable mode for high-contrast-critical surfaces.
Migration approach: preserve legacy visual output at the component boundary where possible by providing a compatibility alias layer; opt-in components can adopt new contour tokens progressively.
implementation_notes: Figma: build token page with contour tokens and chromatic ramp; publish as versioned library. Link: https://www.figma.com/file/REDACTED/design-tokens-contour

Tokens export: ensure tokens.json follows the schema used by token-transformer (tokens -> css-vars, tokens -> scss map, tokens -> tokens.json). Example repo path: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-tokens/tree/contour
Migration map: create CSV mapping legacy token -> contour token + fallback CSS var. Store: /confluence/design/contour-migration

Component work: coordinate with ENG to add feature flag 'use_contour_tokens' and implement a small runtime shim that swaps CSS variables for flagged routes. Avoid repeating heavy runtime work by applying substitution at the build step for Server-Side Rendered pages.
Testing: add Percy visual tests for impacted components and a contrast automation job to run against the storybook builds. Define thresholds for allowable deltas.
Performance: keep token count under 120 values for initial rollout to avoid large CSS payload; consider generating density-specific stylesheets to reduce overrides.
